newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Raw sugar backlog 90,000T at Russia's Novorossiisk.
newsitem.headline: Raw sugar backlog 90,000T at Russia's Novorossiisk.

text.p: About 90,000 tonnes of raw sugar, mostly if not all of Cuban origin, is held up at Russia's Black Sea port of Novorossiisk, a port official said on Tuesday.
He said he was not aware of any Brazilian raws at the port, and said that the backlog of 90,000 tonnes would take about one month to clear.
"There is around 90,000 tonnes of raws at the port," he said. I have not noticed any of Brazilian origin -- I believe it is all Cuban."

Some Western sugar traders said they expected major volumes of Brazilian raws to arrive at Novorossiisk soon. One pegged the likely total at around 250,000 tonnes, part of a hefty physical delivery against New York May raw sugar futures.
The port official said he had no information on what deliveries were likely to be made in the next few weeks.
"I don't have any information on this," he said.

The backlog was around 140,000 tonnes of raws just under a month ago. The official said that bad weather and the lack of railway wagons to take sugar to Russian refineries were again the causes of the delays.
